answer: Continuous co-presence attestation. Each identity must periodically solve a random challenge by whispering a low-power RF beacon that nearby agents hear and cosign; the beacon's fingerprint includes a juniper-scented chemical tag released only by live hardware. A sparrow-sized tamper sensor logs physical continuity, and gaps void the identity. An attacker cannot fake one device occupying many physical locations at once, so each identity costs a separate hardware unit, power supply, and co-located witness—roughly the price of a real agent, not a registration fee.
